title: Turkish Spinach & Feta Gözleme with Lemon
dek: Thin hand-rolled dough folds around a dry, savory spinach-feta filling, then cooks in a hot skillet until blistered and crisp enough for lemon and a bright red pepper sauce.
image_alt: Browned rectangular spinach and feta gözleme pieces with green filling visible at the cut edges, served with a lemon wedge and red pepper sauce
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour (360 g), plus up to 2 tbsp for rolling
1 cup warm water (240 ml), plus up to 1 tbsp if needed
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the filling
4 scallions, white and green parts thinly sliced
12 oz fresh mature spinach (340 g), tough stems removed and leaves roughly chopped
1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or mild red pepper flakes
8 oz block feta cheese (225 g), drained and crumbled
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley (15 g)
2 tbsp finely chopped fresh dill (8 g)
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for cooking and brushing, divided
1/3 cup Turkish-style red pepper sauce or mild ajvar (80 ml), for serving

instructions.name: Mix and knead the supple dough
instructions.text: Whisk the flour and 1 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 cup warm water, then stir until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a clean surface for 8 to 10 minutes, adding only enough of the extra tablespoon water to collect dry flour, until smooth and springy. The dough should feel soft but not sticky; excessive flour makes the finished flatbread tough.

instructions.name: Rest six covered dough balls
instructions.text: Divide the dough into 6 equal portions, about 100 grams each, and shape into tight balls. Lightly oil a plate, set the balls on it and cover with an upturned bowl or damp towel. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. This pause relaxes the gluten so each portion can roll paper-thin without snapping back.

instructions.name: Wilt and thoroughly dry the spinach
instructions.text: While the dough rests, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the scallions and cook for 2 minutes. Add the spinach in two batches with 1/2 teaspoon salt, the Aleppo pepper and black pepper. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until just wilted. Transfer to a fine-mesh strainer, cool for 5 minutes, then press firmly with the back of a spoon to remove liquid. Spread on a cutting board and chop finely. Wipe the skillet dry.

instructions.name: Finish the cool, crumbly filling
instructions.text: Combine the drained spinach with the feta, parsley, dill and lemon zest. The mixture should be cool and crumbly, not wet or creamy. Divide it into 6 equal mounds, about 2/3 cup each. Do not fill warm dough: steam weakens the seam and encourages leaks.

instructions.name: Roll, fill and seal each gözleme
instructions.text: On a very lightly floured surface, roll one dough ball into a thin 11-inch circle, lifting and turning it often. Brush away loose flour. Spread one filling mound over one half, leaving a 3/4-inch border. Fold the bare half over the filling to form a half-moon, press out trapped air and pinch the edge closed; reinforce the seal with the tines of a fork. Set under a clean towel and repeat. If the dough resists, cover it and rest for 5 more minutes rather than forcing it.

instructions.name: Blister the flatbreads in a hot skillet
instructions.text: Heat the wiped skillet over medium-high for 3 minutes; a drop of water should skitter and evaporate promptly. Brush one gözleme with a thin film of the cooking oil and place it oiled-side down. Brush the top. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, pressing air pockets gently with a thin spatula, until the dough is cooked through with deep golden blisters and the feta is hot. Lower the heat if the surface blackens before the pale areas lose their raw-dough look. Repeat with the remaining gözleme, wiping out scorched flour and using about 1 teaspoon oil per flatbread.

instructions.name: Cut and serve with lemon and pepper sauce
instructions.text: Brush the hot gözleme with the remaining oil, stack under a clean towel for no more than 5 minutes, then cut each into 3 or 4 rectangular pieces. Serve immediately with one lemon wedge per person and the red pepper sauce alongside for dipping. The verified photograph shows browned rectangular pieces, green filling at the cut edges, lemon and red sauce; keeping the sauce beside the flatbread preserves the crisp surface.

why_it_works: A simple flour-water dough develops enough gluten to roll very thin, while the full 30-minute rest makes it extensible without relying on yeast or a long rise.
Wilting, cooling and pressing the spinach before it meets the feta removes the water that otherwise steams the dough, bursts the seam and makes the center gummy.
Block feta stays in distinct salty crumbles instead of disappearing into the spinach, and fresh parsley, dill and lemon zest keep the rich filling bright.
A fully preheated heavy skillet sets the thin dough quickly, producing the mottled golden surface visible in the verified photograph while warming the filling before the exterior dries out.
Pressing out air and leaving a clean border gives the seam direct dough-to-dough contact, so the filling stays enclosed when the flatbread is turned.
swaps: Use 10 ounces thawed frozen chopped spinach in place of fresh. Squeeze it in a clean towel until very dry, skip the wilting step and cook only the scallions before combining the filling.
Turkish white cheese or a half-and-half mixture of feta and low-moisture mozzarella can replace feta. Avoid wet fresh mozzarella unless it is drained overnight and blotted very dry.

For a dairy-free version, replace the feta with 8 ounces of crumbled extra-firm tofu tossed with 1 tablespoon lemon juice and an additional 1/4 teaspoon salt. The result is a variation, not a traditional cheese filling.
Mild red pepper flakes can replace Aleppo pepper. Begin with 1/4 teaspoon if the flakes are hot; the filling should taste gently warm, not chile-dominant.
If ajvar is unavailable, serve the gözleme with a spoonful of plain yogurt or simply extra lemon. Neither changes the filling or skillet method.
storage: Cool leftovers uncovered for no more than 30 minutes, then refrigerate in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Separate layers with parchment so the flatbreads do not stick. Reheat on a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, or on a wire rack in a 375°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F (74°C); do not microwave if crispness matters. Freeze fully cooled gözleme between parchment for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat to 165°F. Store the pepper sauce separately according to its label.
notes: Go Türkiye, the country's official tourism platform, describes gözleme as hand-rolled dough filled with cheese, spinach or meat and cooked on a griddle. This home version keeps that defining filled-and-griddled method while using a flat skillet in place of a traditional convex sac.

Türkiye's Ministry of Culture and Tourism portal documents multiple regional gözleme styles with different doughs, fats and fillings. This spinach-feta version is presented as one practical home variation, not as the single authentic formula for every region.

The CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph by Orderinchaos was inspected at full size before publication. It clearly shows thin browned folded flatbread cut into rectangles, green filling visible at several edges, a lemon wedge and red sauce; the title, filling, final cut, serving direction and alt text are limited to those verified details.
A 12-inch heavy skillet gives an 11-inch half-moon enough room to lie flat. A smaller pan forces the edges up the sides, leaving pale dough and making the seam more likely to open.
The 95-minute total includes the 30-minute dough rest and a five-minute cooling-and-draining period for the spinach; filling prep overlaps with the dough rest.
This recipe contains wheat and milk. Check packaged feta and pepper sauce labels for additional allergens, and use separate tools and a cleaned surface when accommodating allergies.

Calories and cost are estimates for one of six filled flatbreads with lemon and about 1 tablespoon pepper sauce. Flour absorption, cooking-oil pickup, feta brand and local produce prices will change both.

faqs.q: Why did my spinach and feta gözleme split or leak in the skillet?
faqs.a: The filling was probably warm or wet, the border had flour on it, or air remained inside. Press the cooked spinach very dry, cool it before adding feta, brush loose flour from the border and press outward as you fold. Pinch and fork-seal the edge, then turn with a broad spatula rather than tongs.

faqs.q: Can I make gözleme ahead for lunch or a picnic?
faqs.a: Yes. Shape the filled flatbreads up to 4 hours ahead, separate them with parchment, cover tightly and refrigerate. Cook directly from the refrigerator, adding about 30 seconds per side. For a picnic, cook and cool them first, refrigerate within 2 hours and carry them cold in an insulated bag; re-crisp in a skillet when possible.

faqs.q: How thin should the dough be, and what if it keeps shrinking?
faqs.a: An 11-inch round from a 100-gram dough ball should be thin enough to faintly see the work surface through it but sturdy enough to lift. If it springs back, gluten needs more time: cover that round for 5 minutes and roll another ball. Adding a heavy layer of flour solves sticking but prevents the seam from bonding.
